This aligns with historical May averages near 29–32°C and the plum rain season's typical effect of limiting peaks below recent heatwave levels. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest official guidance from PAGASA indicates a 90% chance of rain and maximum temperatures near 33°C for Manila on May 30 under easterly flow and increased cloud cover, which has anchored trader consensus around 33–35°C. Afternoon thunderstorms typical of the late dry season could cap heating if they develop early, while delayed convection or clearer breaks would allow peaks to 34–35°C given climatological afternoon warming. Ensemble models show modest spread on moisture timing and boundary-layer mixing, creating genuine uncertainty that narrows the gap between the top three outcomes. Historical May maxima near 34°C provide baseline context, but the elevated rain probability this weekend remains the dominant near-term driver.
